title: The keyboard of the unbounded mouse appears in the latest version and cannot be used synchronously between two computers

judgment.rationale: The body mentions two computers, campus Wi-Fi versus Ethernet, and a built-in laptop keyboard, while the live labels name ZoomIt and Keyboard Manager. It never identifies which PowerToys feature is being used or which computer loses input. That ambiguity prevents selecting a PowerToys code owner.
evidence: The report says the computers could control each other before version 0.90 and now cannot do so reliably.
It also says a laptop's built-in keyboard may stop working, but the expected and actual behavior fields are blank.
The issue is labeled for ZoomIt and Keyboard Manager, has no comments, assignees, or linked work.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask which feature and machine are affected and request a minimal two-computer reproduction.

fix_assessment.rationale: The affected feature and failing machine are not identified, so a PowerToys code fix cannot yet be assessed.

issue_context.summary: The reporter describes loss of keyboard/mouse control between two computers after an update, plus a possible local laptop keyboard failure, without identifying the feature or affected side.
known_information: The reported versions are 0.90 and 0.90.1 from Microsoft Store.
The computers can connect over Ethernet but not directly over campus IPv4 Wi-Fi.
The issue is labeled ZoomIt and Keyboard Manager, not Mouse Without Borders.
inferences: The report may concern a cross-device feature, but the label and symptom do not establish which module is involved.
A local built-in keyboard failure may be distinct from the inter-computer control problem.
issue_context.analysis: Before asking for diagnostics or choosing a source path, the reporter needs to identify the feature, direction of control, and which keyboard becomes unusable. Those answers distinguish a local hook problem from a cross-device connectivity or input-forwarding problem.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live body and confirmed the thread has no comments.
Checked live labels, assignees, and linked timeline references; no linked work was found.
The only labeled source areas are ZoomIt and Keyboard Manager, while the described cross-device behavior does not identify either one.

information_gaps.information: Which PowerToys feature is used for the two-computer control and which computer's built-in keyboard stops working.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether the issue belongs to a local keyboard hook, a remote-control module, or another component.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Name the feature as shown in PowerToys Settings and state whether the failure is on the local computer, remote computer, or both.

information_gaps.information: A short sequence showing the before/after behavior, including connection method and direction of keyboard and mouse control.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a network-connectivity regression from keyboard input being intercepted or lost locally.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Provide numbered steps for one local/remote pair and state whether the same failure occurs over Ethernet and campus Wi-Fi.

comment.body:
Thanks for noting that the two PCs could control each other before version 0.90, that Ethernet works where campus Wi-Fi does not, and that a laptop's built-in keyboard may also stop working. The issue is labeled ZoomIt and Keyboard Manager, but the report does not say which feature provides the cross-PC control or which PC loses input.

Please provide:
1. The PowerToys feature shown in Settings and whether the built-in keyboard failure is on the local PC or the remote PC.
2. Numbered steps showing the connection method and which direction keyboard/mouse control fails.

These details distinguish a local Keyboard Manager problem from a cross-device connection or forwarding problem.
